title: Sales enablement playbook: positioning, competitive briefs, pricing guidance, pitch decks, case studies, and security FAQ
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook is the canonical sales enablement reference for Redwood Inference product positioning and GTM messaging used by field reps, solutions engineers, and partner teams. It consolidates: value propositions for buyer personas, competitive brief(s), objection-handling, pricing guidance and sample ROI math, a recommended pitch-deck outline, two short case studies with talking points, and a prospect-facing Security & Privacy FAQ. Use this doc for enablement sessions, deal planning, and as the base for tailored customer collateral.

Audience:
- Sales (AE/SE)
- Solutions Engineering
- Channel/Partner teams
- Marketing (demand/gen, content)

Key takeaways (elevator):
- Redwood Inference: a developer-first inference platform focused on predictable, production-grade LLM serving across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments.
- Primary buyer outcomes: lower unit cost for inference, consistent latency and reliability, and deployment flexibility to meet security/regulatory needs.
- Differentiators: production-first runtime optimizations, unified operations across environments, and cost-aware performance controls.

1) Positioning and Messaging (by persona)

Executive summary message (for decision-makers):
- Headline: Ship LLM features at production scale with predictable costs and SLAs.
- Subhead: Redwood combines a GPU-optimized serving runtime, model lifecycle tools, and routing/observability to deliver reliable, low-latency inference that lowers per-token costs and operational risk.

Developer / Platform Engineer:
- Pain: inconsistent latency, expensive token costs, and complex ops for scaling LLMs.
- Message: Redwood offers a single API and SDKs that let engineering teams move from prototype to production with predictable latency, batching and caching controls, and transparent performance profiles per model.
- Proof points: streaming + function calling, search-optimized embeddings, documented performance profiles, and sample SDK code (see Appendix).

ML/Infrastructure Lead:
- Pain: model ops complexity, quantization and kernel choices, KV cache management, and unpredictable throughput under mixed workloads.
- Message: Redwood’s serving runtime automatically selects kernels and batching policies, supports quantized model variants, and provides dedicated GPU pools with autoscaling for predictable throughput.
- Proof points: Dedicated capacity with SLA, per-route latency dashboards, and rollback/AB rollout features in Redwood Console.

Security/Compliance Officer:
- Pain: data residency, auditability, and key management.
- Message: Private deployment options (VPC & on-prem) and KMS/HSM integrations provide audit logs, tenant isolation, and retention controls needed for regulated workloads.

2) Value proposition matrix (short bullets)

- Cost: intelligent batching/caching, model quantization recommendations, and predictable reserved capacity to lower per-token costs by 30–60% on typical production workloads.
- Latency: optimized kernels, continuous batching with latency SLOs, and auto-fallback routes to maintain p95 targets.
- Reliability: multi-tier fallbacks (model variants, region, capacity tier) + SLA for Dedicated customers.
- Developer velocity: single API across deployment modes, sample apps and SDKs, and a catalog of vetted models with performance profiles.

3) Competitive brief (summary vs common alternatives)

Competitors referenced: OpenAI, Anthropic, major cloud managed endpoints (AWS Bedrock/GDM, GCP Vertex AI), self-hosted runtimes (KServe, llm-serving vendors).

Key comparison pillars:
- Performance economics: Redwood emphasizes per-token cost controls and workload-aware batching vs many competitors that expose only raw model pricing.
- Operational model: Redwood unifies hosted, dedicated, and private with the same API and console — competitors often split features between managed and self-hosted offerings.
- Runtime optimizations: Redwood’s kernel selection, KV cache, and quantization profiles target production latencies; self-hosted stacks may require customer engineering to match.
- Security & compliance: Redwood Private + KMS/HSM, audit logs, and onboarding checklists tailored for enterprise compliance.

Short rebuttals / objection handling:
- "OpenAI models are easier/better": Acknowledge model quality parity for many tasks, then reframe: if you need predictable SLOs, unit economics, or private deployments with auditability, Redwood reduces operational risk and hidden costs.
- "We can self-host and save money": Quantify TCO — include ops headcount, reliability risk cost, and the engineering time to optimize kernels and batching. Redwood’s Dedicated contract and Optimize tooling frequently deliver lower total cost of ownership for production traffic.
- "Cloud vendor managed endpoints tie into our infra": Redwood supports regional deployments and integrations; for customers committed to a single cloud, Redwood provides a Private deployment package and co-located Dedicated options.

4) Pricing guidance and sample ROIs

Pricing constructs (sales guidance):
- Hosted API (self-serve): per-token pricing for generation and embeddings (list price guidance). Encourage usage of tiered discounts for high-volume customers and recommend Reserved Credits for predictable spend.
- Dedicated: monthly reserved capacity with commit levels (e.g., small/medium/large GPU pools) priced by throughput and SLA. Typical contract length: 12–36 months.
- Private: platform license + deployment fee + optional managed services and support tiers.
- Add-ons: enhanced observability retention, compliance packages, premium SLAs, and dedicated support.

Sample ROI (sales play):
- Assumptions: customer has 200M tokens/month, current cost = $0.08 per 1k tokens (managed endpoint + infra + ops), latency p95 = 600ms, 2 full-time engineers maintaining ops.
- Redwood Hosted/Optimize scenario: per-1k-token cost reduced to $0.05 via batching/caching and model recommendations; latency improved to p95 = 200ms; eliminate 1 ops FTE.
- Rapid ROI: monthly savings on tokens = (0.08-0.05) * 200,000 = $6,000. Ops salary reduction (pro-rated) = $8,333/mo. Total monthly benefit = $14,333 -> payback on integration + ramp in < 3 months for typical onboarding.

Pricing conversation playbook:
1. Understand token volume and latency requirements.
2. Recommend Hosted if customer wants fast time-to-value; recommend Dedicated for predictable throughput and lower unit economics; recommend Private when compliance requires VPC/on-prem.
3. Propose pilot (30 days or 1 quarter) with clear success metrics: cost per 1k tokens, p50/p95 latency, error rate, and ops handoff milestones.

5) Pitch deck outline (recommended slide flow)

Use the following slide structure for standard 12–15 slide deck:
1. Title / Hook (customer logo)
2. The problem (latency/cost/ops complexity)
3. Market context (brief LLM landscape)
4. Redwood value prop (one-liner + bullets)
5. Deployment options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
6. Architecture (high-level diagram showing routing, caching, Dedicated pools)
7. Performance & cost benchmarks (model profiles, p95 numbers, batching benefits)
8. Security & compliance (audit logs, KMS, data residency)
9. Case studies / references
10. Pricing & pilot proposal
11. Roadmap & integration plan
12. Appendix: API examples, SDK snippets, SSO/KMS onboarding notes

Presentation tips for SEs:
- Start with business outcomes (latency, cost, time-to-market).
- Bring a short demo or replay of perf dashboards for live proof.
- Tailor language for persona: exec-focused decks for economic wins, infra-focused for runtime details.

6) Case studies (short-talk tracks)

Case study A: AI-native customer (SaaS personalization)
- Situation: Customer had an LLM-based personalization pipeline serving 20k users/day, inconsistent latency and spiky costs.
- Redwood action: Deployed Dedicated pool, enabled prefix and KV caching, and applied quantization profile for their transformer variant.
- Outcome: p95 latency dropped 3x (600ms -> 200ms), cost per 1k tokens reduced 45%, and team removed 1.5 FTEs worth of ops work.
- Talking points: show before/after graphs, highlight Dedicated SLA, emphasize rollout/rollback simplicity.

Case study B: Regulated enterprise (financial services)
- Situation: Must keep customer data in-region and maintain audit trails for inference requests.
- Redwood action: Private deployment in customer VPC, KMS integration, and extended retention for audit logging.
- Outcome: Passed internal security audit, enabled production rollout, and reduced time-to-market by 6 weeks relative to building an internal solution.
- Talking points: emphasize compliance checklist, audit-proof architecture, and HLD for on-prem packaging.

7) Security FAQ (candidate prospect-facing questions and short answers)

Q: Where does data get stored and for how long?
A: For Hosted customers, default retention is 30 days for logs; payloads are encrypted in transit and at rest. For Dedicated and Private, data residency is configurable (regional deployments or customer-managed VPC/on-prem) and retention settings are customer-controlled.

Q: How does Redwood handle key management?
A: Redwood integrates with customer KMS providers; for Private deployments we support HSM-backed keys and bring-your-own-key configurations.

Q: Do you provide audit logs and traceability for inference requests?
A: Yes. Redwood Console provides request-level tracing and immutable audit logs. Additional retention is an add-on.

Q: What certifications/attestations do you hold?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is engaged in ISO 27001 readiness for Private customers. We provide compliance evidence packages on onboarding.

Q: How do you isolate tenant workloads?
A: Isolation depends on deployment mode: Hosted uses tenant-level logical isolation plus strict RBAC and network controls; Dedicated provides GPU pool isolation per customer; Private provides full network and control-plane separation.

Q: What is your vulnerability management process?
A: Regular internal scans, third-party penetration tests annually, and a CVE triage process with SLA for security patches for Dedicated and Private customers.

Appendix: Useful snippets and assets

- Example curl (token generation):
curl -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.5-instruct", "input":"Summarize the following...", "max_tokens":200}'

- Integration checklist (suggested pilot success metrics):
  - Token volume sample & target per-1k-token cost
  - Latency p50/p95 targets
  - Error rate threshold (e.g., <1%)
  - Observability handoff: dashboards and alerts configured
  - Security sign-offs: KMS/SSO configured and audit logs validated

- Sales assets to attach to deal package:
  - Benchmarks: curated model profiles and performance charts
  - Pitch deck (editable deck)
  - Technical one-pager for SEs
  - Onboarding checklist for Dedicated/Private deployments

Owner and escalation
- Document owner: Go-to-market / Enablement (Asha Patel)
- Technical reviewer: Eng Platform (Liam Chen)

Maintenance cadence
- Quarterly review of messaging and pricing guidance.
- Benchmarks and model profiles updated monthly or when a new model variant is adopted.
